Week 3 · Skills · 12
Habit
Your own skill
The habit
If you type it twice, make it a skill
You test something, you need the same setup again, so you explain it again. Stop. Make it a small skill so you never write it twice.
Pain point
Same long prompt, again
SKILL.md
Write the steps once
/test-checkout
Run it next time
Improve
Fix it when it misses
Good candidates
Seeding test data, release checklists, a log-in-and-check flow
Rule of thumb
Third time you type it, it becomes a skill
Share it
Commit .claude/skills/ so the team gets it too
Week 3 · Skills · 13
Habit
Skill
Example
A skill written from a pain point
Your old prompt, saved as a recipe:
disable-model-invocation means it only runs when you call it
$ARGUMENTS passes the base URL
allowed-tools skips the approval prompt for the seed script
.claude/skills/test-checkout/SKILL.md
---
name: test-checkout
description: Smoke-test checkout as the test user
argument-hint: [base-url]
disable-model-invocation: true
allowed-tools: Bash(npm run seed:test-user)
---
1. Run npm run seed:test-user
2. Open $ARGUMENTS/login (default localhost:3000)
3. Log in with the test user from .env.test
4. Add one product and open /checkout
5. Report console errors and failed requests

Week 3 · Orca ADE · 36
Scale solution
Desktop app
What real users say
Three things to plan for
Quota × N
Three agents in parallel use your Claude quota about three times as fast.
Conflicts are still git
Worktrees stop overwrites, not clashing changes. Split work into independent tasks.
You still review
Orca makes review faster. It does not make review optional.

Week 3 · Case studies · 38
Scale solution
Case study
Case 1 · Fan-out on an open design question
Generate three answers, judge one
Rick Hightower
Claude Certified Architect, ex Senior Distinguished Engineer
Task: add authentication, with no clear best approach. Instead of guessing, he dispatched three attempts and picked one.
Wall-clock: one agent's runtime, not three
Human time: three diff reviews
Swap --agent to run Claude Code on any attempt
fan out, walk away, pick one
orca worktree create --name auth-jwt \
  --agent codex --prompt "short-lived JWTs"
orca worktree create --name auth-session ...
orca worktree create --name auth-oauth ...
# later, from a terminal or your phone
orca worktree ps --json
orca terminal wait --terminal <id> --for tui-idle
# review diffs in the GUI, keep the winner
orca worktree rm --worktree name:auth-session
Source: rickhigh.substack.com, Orca and the Rise of the ADE (Aug 2026)

AGENTS.md rules for their own agents (paraphrased)
- Every change must work over SSH
- Not every workspace is a git worktree
- Never follow subagent paths back
  into the main repo
- No files named helpers, utils, common
- Never disable the max-lines lint
Week 3 · Case studies · 42
Scale solution
Case study
What the case studies agree on
Four lessons before you scale up
Review is the ceiling
You can launch fifty agents. You cannot really review fifty diffs.
Supervise fewer
Start with two or three. Raise it only when review keeps up.
Split by file ownership
One team saw 43% merge conflicts in parallel; 0% once same-module tasks ran in order.
Spec first
Output is bounded by how clearly you said what done means.
A strong reviewer with a fleet ships more good code. A weak reviewer ships the same mistakes, faster.
Source: rickhigh.substack.com; conflict numbers from indiekitai/claude-orchestrator README
